The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T03:52:14Z {alert_raised}
Somebody was paged: an on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-11T03:46:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-11T03:54:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 8 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 36 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T03:55:11Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 26.5% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 38.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 25.5% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9916666666666666% {series_before} before it began, 26.5% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 38.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 5,182.30 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T03:52:35Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T03:52:47Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T03:52:47Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T03:52:53Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 03:52:14 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T03:52:58Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T03:52:59Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 03:46 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T03:53:00Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T03:53:01Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 11 03:47 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T03:53:01Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T03:53:02Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 8 {T10.2} minutes before 03:52 {T10.3}
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T03:53:02Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 35 {T11.2} log lines
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T03:53:02Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T12.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T03:53:03Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T03:53:03Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T03:53:03Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 03:53:03 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T03:53:07Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T03:53:08Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T03:53:15Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T03:53:22Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 03:54 {T19.2} - up to 164s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T03:55:11Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 03:54 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-11T03:55:11Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-11T03:55:11Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [monthly-spend-feature] OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-11T03:56:44Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/552

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-11T03:46:28Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 2 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 2 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 03:44–03:45 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 3 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 2 {G46bc.2} minutes, 03:44–03:45 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 9 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 03:44–03:52 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 38.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 28.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 03:47 {Gbac1.7}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 {G971b.1} / on 102 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 03:46 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 03:46–03:52 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 03:47–03:52 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-11T03:46:28Z {C1.1}. That enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% {C1.2} to about 30% {C1.3}. No deployment was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.95 {C1.4}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by `len(bought_this_month)`, the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. Most shoppers have bought before but not this month. For them that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. That is the line the incident log names (spend_summary.py:47). Turning on monthly-spend-feature sent the account page's figure through this function, and every request for such a shopper failed.
      
      The flag was what triggered the incident, but the fault is in the code: the function has no answer for the normal case of a shopper who has bought nothing this month. With the fix, when there are no purchases this month the function returns 0 {F1.1}, because a shopper with no purchases this month has spent nothing this month. Otherwise it divides as before. Shoppers who did buy this month get the same result as before.
      
      Other code is unchanged. With the flag off, `render_spend_summary` still uses `average_spend_per_item`, and that function still raises for an account with no purchases at all. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py expect that error, and that error is the only case the line-number test in test_account_page.py checks. Nothing in this change catches errors.
      
      The tests: the new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py call `average_spend_per_item_this_month` and `render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True)` for a shopper whose purchases all fall outside the current month, and assert 0 {F1.2}. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #552 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The function the flag turned on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, divides the account's total spent this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month` and has no answer for an empty list. For any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError at the line the logs name, so every account page request for such a shopper failed once monthly-spend-feature sent the page's spend figure through it. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new feature made the account page use a new monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month because it ends up dividing by zero.
still_at_risk: Code-Fix's reading says the faulty calculation was still in the code: switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month, and with the flag off, the older calculation can still fail for accounts with no purchases at all.
symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
causal_chain 1: Shoppers opening their account page got a failed request instead of the page, and the service's share of failed requests rose sharply. (cites AL1; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero, raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The error shows up in the logs from the onset until the logs that were read end. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. The flag's evaluations went from all off, to a mix of on and off at the onset, to all on right after it. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: A deployment: the production change events read back for the day before the onset held only this flag change, and no deploy came back. (cites T9, under "What Argus did, in order"; P1, under "Changes to production it read")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read, and that was this one. (cites T15, under "What Argus did, in order"; P1, under "Changes to production it read")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 3: The client-disconnect failures on the account page: these were seen before the onset, while the account page error rate was still low. The division-by-zero failures appear only once the flag went on. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: With the flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a new monthly per-item average that divides by the number of this month's purchases, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: The flag switch reached all of the account page's traffic at once: its evaluations went from all off to all on almost immediately. No staged rollout and no error-rate check that would halt it were seen.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that halted when errors rose would have exposed only a small share of shoppers, and would have been stopped before it reached all traffic.
contributing_factors 2: Before the flag was switched on in production, no test was seen that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases in the current month.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have raised the division by zero before the flag was turned on, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
action_items 1: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, starting with a small share of traffic, instead of switching them on for all traffic at once.
action_items 2: Halt and revert a staged flag rollout automatically when the service's error rate rises while it is under way.
action_items 3: Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including for shoppers with no purchases in the current month, to pass before that flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 4: Decide whether `average_spend_per_item`, used while the flag is off, should keep raising for an account with no purchases at all. Code-Fix reports that the current tests expect it to raise.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
